newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba harvest slowed but pushing ahead.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba harvest slowed but pushing ahead.

text.p: Wet weather slowed harvest in most of Manitoba in the week ended October 7 but combining was able to pick up late in the period, with mostly average yields, Manitoba Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.

Southwest Manitoba - Snowfall last Tuesday ranged from less than an inch in southern districts to 4-6 inches in the north. Harvest in the south was nearly complete while Minnedosa and Neepawa districts were only 50 and 75 percent complete, respectively. Yields and quality remained good.
Northwest Manitoba - Combining was about 70 percent complete, against 60 percent a week earlier.
"Frosts up to -5 Centigrade were experienced most nights," it said. Harvesting was widespread by Thursday after rain delays earlier.

Central Manitoba - Combining of cereals was about 80 percent complete, against 75 percent a week earlier. The region had two hard frosts in the past week, it said. The Portage area reported some downgrading of wheat to 3CW and Feed after the frosts. Canola was moving well with 75 percent of the crop harvested, it said.

Eastern Manitoba - Cereals were 95 percent combined and canola 90 percent, good gains for the week. Yields were average. Flax was 50 percent harvested with average yields. The first killing frost hit last week, it said.

Interlake region - Cereals were 95 percent harvested against 80 percent last week, canola 95 percent against 75 percent, and flax 60 percent against 50 percent. Yields remained above average. Demand for aeration and drying devices also remained high, it said.
